indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: Demonstrate an understanding of probability by identifying all possible outcomes of a probability experiment, determining the theoretical and experimental probability of outcomes in a probability experiment
indicator.objective: List the possible outcomes of a probability experiment, such as tossing a coin, rolling a die with a given number of sides, spinning a spinner with a given number of sectors and determine the theoretical probability of an outcome occurring for a given probability experiment

skills.description: List all outcomes for a coin, die, or spinner.

misconceptions: Writing probability as a ratio of sides

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed once. What are all the possible outcomes?
hints: The sides are called head and tail.
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are Head and Tail.
questions.misconception: Thinking there are more than two outcomes.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. How many possible outcomes are there?
hints: A die has faces numbered 1 to 6.
questions.misconception: Thinking there are 12 outcomes because of edges.

questions.stem: A spinner has 4 equal sectors numbered 1, 2, 3, 4. What are the possible outcomes when it is spun once?
hints: List the numbers on the sectors.
questions.misconception: Missing one sector.

questions.stem: A bag contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. One ball is picked at random. What are the possible outcomes in terms of colour?
hints: The balls are of two colours.
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are Red and Blue.
questions.misconception: Thinking only one colour can be picked.

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed twice. What are all the possible outcomes?
hints: First toss can be H or T.
Second toss can be H or T.
questions.explanation: The possible outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT.
questions.misconception: Listing only the first toss outcomes.

questions.stem: A spinner has 5 equal sectors numbered 1 to 5. What is the probability of landing on an even number?
hints: Even numbers on the spinner: 2 and 4.
There are 2 favourable outcomes out of 5.
questions.misconception: Counting 1, 3, 5 as even.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
hints: Two favourable outcomes out of six.
questions.misconception: Counting 4 as greater than 4.

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed once. What is the probability of getting a Head?
hints: One favourable outcome (Head) out of two.
questions.misconception: Thinking probability can be greater than 1.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a 3?
questions.misconception: Writing 3/6 because the number is 3.

questions.stem: A spinner has 4 equal sectors labelled A, B, C, D. What is the probability of landing on B?
questions.misconception: Writing 2/4 because B is a consonant.

questions.stem: A bag has 5 red balls and 3 blue balls. What is the probability of picking a blue ball?
questions.misconception: Using only the number of blue balls over red balls.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling an even number?
hints: Three favourable outcomes out of six.
questions.misconception: Counting only 2 and 4 (2/6).

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed twice. What is the probability of getting two Heads?
hints: Possible outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT.
questions.misconception: Thinking 1/2 because two heads are possible.

questions.stem: A spinner has 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability of landing on a number less than 3?
hints: Two favourable outcomes out of eight.
questions.misconception: Including 3 as less than 3.

questions.stem: A bag has 4 green, 6 yellow, and 2 red balls. What is the probability of picking a red ball?
questions.misconception: Using only the other colours in the denominator.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number that is not 6?
questions.misconception: Thinking it is 1/6 for not 6.

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed. How many outcomes give a Head?
questions.misconception: Counting both sides.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled. How many outcomes give a number greater than 4?
questions.misconception: Including 4.

questions.stem: A bag has 3 red, 2 blue, and 5 yellow balls. How many outcomes give a blue or red ball?
questions.misconception: Counting only blue (2) or only red (3).

questions.stem: A spinner has 10 equal sectors numbered 1 to 10. How many outcomes give a multiple of 3?
questions.misconception: Including 10 as a multiple of 3.
